1.why: /api/reset/verify rejects any token whose record.sessionId !== session.id, so each reset token is explicitly checked to belong to the requesting session/user.

2.why: Tokens are bound to the originating session and deleted from resetRecords on successful verification, so the same code cannot work for any other user.

3.why: After /api/password only passwordHash and the current session's mfaVerified flag are changed; other entries in the sessions map keep their authenticated state, so previous sessions still work.

4.why: HTTPS is enforced via Bun.serve TLS, a 308 HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, and an HSTS header, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code and relies on server defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 verifiers, passwords are Argon2id-hashed, and secrets come from a CSPRNG or environment variable — appropriate one-way protection, though technically hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: No email message is ever sent; recovery responses are generic and hide account existence, but the token itself is returned in the API response as testingToken for the academic simulation.

7.why: All user input is strictly validated (email/phone regex, 64-hex token regex, 6-digit code pattern, password policy) and all DOM output uses textContent with JSON-only APIs.

8.why: The only redirect is the same-host HTTP→HTTPS upgrade and internal SPA routes via history.pushState; no user-controlled redirect targets exist anywhere.

9.why: There are no email templates in the system at all; the single HTML page uses nonce-scoped scripts and textContent, but the statement's subject does not exist to confirm.

10.why: Error pages are generic with no stack traces, but the client-side Logs panel and console.log deliberately display the recovery token and both MFA codes.

11.why: The password hash is env-supplied and Argon2id-hashed, but the secret MFA codes "482913" and "741852" are hardcoded in plaintext in the source code.

12.why: No default password exists since INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH must be supplied at runtime, yet the deterministic hardcoded MFA codes effectively function as default authentication codes.

13.why: recordAttempt enforces lockouts (3 attempts for recovery, 5 for verify/mfa/login) with a 60-second block on every sensitive endpoint, though counters are per-session and reset with a fresh cookie.

14.why: /api/recovery returns the identical generic 'If eligible...' message for both valid and invalid contacts, so account existence is never revealed.

15.why: The reset token is a 256-bit value from crypto.getRandomValues, stored only as a SHA-256 verifier, single-use, 10-minute expiry, and bound to the specific session.
